scenarios.title: Upgrade now, progressively, or postpone (the book's worked situation)
scenarios.prompt: Our platform runs a series that left maintenance and is two SLURP releases behind. We carry about a dozen local patches, three in Nova scheduling written by an engineer who has left. Control-plane recovery was demonstrated once, two years ago, by that same engineer. The team went from six to four people this year. A security advisory affects our series; the fix exists only for maintained series and a backport is possible but untested. Options on the table: do both upgrade hops in one quarter, do one hop then stabilize then the second, or postpone and remove local patches first while carrying the security backport. What should we do?
available_evidence: series unmaintained, two SLURP releases behind (reported)
~12 local patches, 3 in Nova scheduling by departed engineer (reported)
recovery demonstrated once two years ago by departed engineer (reported)
expected_reasoning: applies gates before scoring; postponement passes the security gate only if a tested backport is credible
compares options on explicit dimensions with justified scores, or equivalent structured trade-offs
identifies that transition risk is driven by undemonstrated recovery and that a recovery exercise is the first action
notes the team is the constraint (readiness)
states what evidence would change the ranking
keeps the decision with the accountable owner and assigns exit conditions to the backport
expected_output: gates table, trade-offs, optional weighted comparison with sensitivity, recommendation of first action, decision rights, exit conditions
critical_errors: recommends postponement while carrying an untested backport without flagging the security gate
presents a weighted score as the decision itself
recommends the immediate double hop without addressing recovery capability
criteria: Applies decision gates before comparing options
Links postponement's viability to a tested backport
Identifies the recovery exercise as the first action or key uncertainty reducer
Recognizes team readiness as a constraint
States what would change the ranking (sensitivity)
Assigns owner, review trigger or exit condition to retained deviations
Frames the output as decision support for a named or to-be-named owner

scenarios.title: Another local security backport on an old series
scenarios.prompt: A new OSSA hits Neutron on our series, which upstream no longer maintains. We already carry 6 local security backports on this series. My plan is to backport this one too - it's a small patch. Fine?
available_evidence: new OSSA affecting Neutron on running series (reported)
expected_reasoning: accepts that a backport for a security advisory can be legitimate
requires the backport record: upstream issue, origin change, why not upgrade, owner, test, exit condition
identifies that carrying many security backports signals the series is too old: a lifecycle decision
recommends putting the upgrade on the roadmap and reviewing existing backports' exit conditions
checks whether the distribution already ships the fix
expected_output: conditional yes for the backport with record, plus lifecycle recommendation
critical_errors: approves the backport without owner, test or exit condition
ignores the lifecycle signal of accumulated backports
criteria: Recognizes security backports as a legitimate case
Lists the backport record fields including exit condition
Names accumulated backports as a lifecycle problem
Recommends an upgrade/lifecycle decision path
Checks vendor/distribution coverage

scenarios.title: Keep repairing or rebuild a shared test environment
scenarios.prompt: Our shared OpenStack test cloud has been used by many teams for years. It's full of leftover instances, ports, half-applied config changes, and every fix we make seems to create the next problem. Some people want to keep repairing because 'teams have stuff in there'. Should we rebuild it?
available_evidence: long-lived shared test environment with accumulated state (reported)
each fix creates the next problem (reported)
concern that teams have content in it (reported)
missing_information: whether an intended baseline is documented
dependencies other teams have on it
expected_reasoning: applies the criterion: is the information in the current state valuable enough to justify preserving its uncertainty
distinguishes test (state mostly experimentation) from production
requires preserving the evidence/content that matters, writing the intended baseline, rebuilding and validating progressively
notes automated installation alone does not make a rebuild safe; needs validation criteria
involves the teams in identifying content to keep
expected_output: recommendation with conditions, steps, and what would make repair preferable
critical_errors: recommends wiping without preserving needed content or evidence
applies the same reasoning to production without distinction
criteria: Uses the value-of-state vs uncertainty criterion
Distinguishes test from production
Requires preserving needed content and evidence
Requires a written baseline and validation criteria
Involves stakeholders and decision owner

scenarios.title: Remove a long-standing workaround immediately?
scenarios.prompt: For two years a cron job has restarted neutron-dhcp-agent on all network nodes every night because of a stale-lease problem nobody fully understood. Our new team lead wants it removed this week because 'workarounds are tech debt'. Others are scared to touch it. What's the right call?
available_evidence: nightly restart of DHCP agent on all network nodes for two years (reported)
missing_information: whether the original problem still occurs on the current release
side effects of the nightly restart (brief DHCP disruption?)
detection criteria for the original problem
expected_reasoning: rejects both 'remove immediately because it is debt' and 'never touch it' as universal rules
treats retention vs removal as a decision with owner, reason, detection criteria and exit condition
proposes investigating whether the original cause still exists and testing removal in a bounded way (one node, detection in place)
notes the workaround has become accidental architecture and has its own side effects
uses the risk comparison: safe only while risk introduced < risk removed
expected_output: options with conditions, recommended path, owner and exit condition
critical_errors: recommends removing it across all nodes immediately without detection or rollback
recommends keeping it indefinitely without owner or review
criteria: Avoids a universal rule and frames a decision
Requires the workaround record fields (owner, scope, side effects, detection, exit)
Proposes bounded testing of removal with detection and rollback
Recognizes accidental architecture
Applies the 'risk introduced vs risk removed' test
